note: Initializes response_index to 1 for each socket manager, skipping response 0 which is sent at connection time.
Parses TLV input to populate all 11 response slots (indices 0-10) for socket manager 0 with attacker-controlled data pointers and lengths.
Creates a socketpair and assigns the server-side fd to socket manager 0, establishing the connection that curl will use.
Adds the open server socket to the readable fd_set so that fuzz_send_next_response will be called when the client sends data.
Calls fuzz_send_next_response each time the client socket becomes readable, driving the response sending loop.
Reads the response data pointer at the current response_index. For indices 1 through 10 this is valid, but when response_index reaches 11 this is an out-of-bounds read.
Increments response_index after sending each response. After sending response at index 10, response_index becomes 11.

The bounds check uses '>' instead of '>='. When response_index equals 11 (TLV_MAX_NUM_RESPONSES), the first condition is false, so it evaluates sman->responses[11].data which is out of bounds since the array has only 11 elements (indices 0-10). This triggers the UBSan out-of-bounds read.
